definition: next to or adjoining something
example: The new school was built adjacent to the community park.

definition: although; even though
example: The project was completed on time, albeit with a smaller budget than planned.

definition: to gather together, or to fit parts together to make a whole
example: Workers assemble the final product on a fast-moving production line.

definition: to fall down or fail suddenly and completely
example: Several small businesses collapsed during the economic downturn.

definition: a person one works with, especially in a profession
example: Good relationships with colleagues can improve workplace satisfaction.

definition: to collect information from different sources and put it together
example: Researchers compiled data from over fifty countries for the study.

definition: to form an idea or plan in the mind
example: The policy was originally conceived as a temporary measure.

definition: to persuade someone that something is true
example: It can be difficult to convince people to change long-standing habits.

definition: to lower the level or activity of something, or to make someone feel sad
example: High unemployment can depress consumer spending across the economy.

definition: to unexpectedly experience or be faced with something
example: New employees often encounter difficulties adjusting to workplace culture.

definition: very large in size, amount, or extent
example: Cities face an enormous challenge in managing population growth.

definition: about to happen or be made available soon
example: Details about the forthcoming policy changes will be released next month.

definition: to tend toward a particular opinion or action
example: Younger consumers are more inclined to shop online than in physical stores.

definition: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
example: Employers value integrity as much as technical skill.

definition: belonging naturally to something; essential
example: Many people believe education has an intrinsic value beyond just improving job prospects.

definition: to cite or appeal to something as an authority or justification
example: The government invoked emergency powers to respond to the crisis.

definition: to impose a tax or fee
example: The city levies an additional tax on short-term rentals.

definition: in the same way; similarly
example: Public transport has improved in the capital; likewise, smaller cities have seen investment.

definition: in spite of that; nevertheless
example: The plan is ambitious; nonetheless, it has strong public support.

definition: in spite of; despite
example: Notwithstanding the extra cost, most residents supported the new recycling scheme.

definition: unusual or unexpected
example: It seems odd that such a wealthy country still has high levels of poverty.

definition: continuing to happen or develop
example: The ongoing debate over university tuition fees shows no sign of ending.

definition: a small group of people chosen to discuss or decide something
example: An expert panel was asked to review the safety of the new drug.

definition: to continue firmly despite difficulty or opposition
example: Gender inequality in pay continues to persist in many industries.

definition: to present or constitute a problem or risk
example: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal cities.

definition: unwillingness to do something
example: There is growing reluctance among young people to take on long-term debt.

definition: used to express doubt about whether a name or term is accurate
example: The so-called solution did little to address the root of the problem.

definition: uncomplicated and easy to understand or do
example: The application process was straightforward and took only a few minutes.

definition: to experience or be subjected to a process or change
example: The company underwent major restructuring after the merger.

definition: by which; through which
example: The government introduced a scheme whereby small businesses could apply for emergency loans.
